postings.description: AMENDMENT A0001 Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice REQUEST FOR SF 330 36C25227Q0013 Project 578-27-003: Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1 (AE) Design/Engineering Services SF-330 Package Due: October 30, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. CST (see details below) Points of Contact: Donita.Grace@va.gov INTRODUCTION: THIS IS A TOTAL 100% SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) SET-ASIDE in accordance with Public Law 109-461. This is a Request for SF330s for Architect/Engineer (A/E) Design Services for Project Number 578-27-003: Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1 (AE) at the Edward J. Hines VA Hospital in Hines, IL. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO SOLICITATION PACKAGE WILL BE ISSUED via SAM.gov. A request for proposal will be issued directly to the top-rated firm for which negotiations will commence in accordance with FAR part 36. The anticipated A/E design services, to be awarded, will be procured in accordance with the Selection of Architects and Engineers Act (Public Law 92- 582), FAR Part 36.6 and VA Acquisition Regulation 836.6. Period of Performance: 449 Calendar Days Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 NAICS Code: 541310 Size Standard: $12.5 Million SBA & SAM : in accordance with VAAR 819.7003, at the time of SF330 submission and prior to award of any contract, the offeror must represent to the contracting officer that it is a (1) SDVOSB eligible firm; (2) Small business concern under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to the acquisition; and (3) SDVOSB listed as verified in SBA at: https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/ Additionally, all eligible firms must be registered and current in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be evaluated and eligible for contract award. If the firm is not registered in SAM, you may register online at https://www.sam.gov. 1. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Offeror shall provide a minimum of three (3), and no more than five (5) recent and relevant Government and private experience projects similar in size, scope, and complexity, and experience with the type of projects/competence above. Relevant is defined as those task requirements identified in the Statement of Work. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. At a minimum, include the following for each submitted project (if applicable): Project title, location, contract number, and detailed narrative describing the scope of services provided including the type of work performed by the offeror and its role in the project i.e., prime contract, Teaming Partner, or subcontractor. Project Owner, owner s point of contact including telephone number and email address. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. To demonstrate technical competence, the offeror shall include narratives of how the firm addresses each of the following topics. Simply restating this list will not be sufficient. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards. FACTOR 2: PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 2A: Key Positions (15 Points). Subfactor 2B: SDVOSB Compliance (5 Points). The architects and engineers on the firm s staff representing the project or signing/stamping drawings in each discipline must possess a minimum of five (5) years of experience and are required to be licensed, registered, or certified by a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory. Provide professional license jurisdiction of issue and license numbers and/or proof of licensure. A resume for each of these key positions must be provided, corresponding with the title matching the disciplines listed for the project. At a minimum, the offeror must describe the professional qualifications and specific experience in the required disciplines within the past five (5) years. Key positions and disciplines required for this project include, but are not limited to: Project Manager Architect Mechanical Engineer Electrical Engineer Plumbing Engineer Structural Engineer Interior Designer The evaluation will consider education, certifications, training, registration, overall and relevant experience and longevity with the firm. Offer must include the following statement of SDVOSB compliance when submitting the personnel proposed to perform the work under this requirement: I [signatory authority] ______________________, [company] _____________________; certify that the team proposed to perform under this requirement demonstrates the capability of 50% SDVOSB performance in compliance of 48 CFR 852.219-10. FACTOR 3: PAST PERFORMANCE (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 3A: Past Performance of projects identified in FACTOR 1. (15 Points). Subfactor 3B: Average Past Performance of all projects (5 Points). Provide CPARS data for all projects identified in FACTOR 1. For any project that does NOT have CPARS data available, a Past Performance Questionnaire (PPQ) is required to be submitted with the SF330. Please utilize the attached PPQ document. CPARS data and PPQs will not be included in the page count. All projects provided in the SF330 must be completed by the office/ branch/ individual team member performing the work under this contract. The following information must be clearly specified on each performance report: Contract/task order number Project title Prime firm Start date Completion date Offers shall only include CPARS data for the projects listed in FACTOR 1. The contracting officer shall directly retrieve CPARS reviews from www.CPARS.gov to determine average past performance of previous projects. Government Past Performance Information Systems may be accessed. Evaluating past performance and experience may include information provided by the firm, customer inquiries, Government databases, publicly available sources, and additional projects in CPARS. Failure to provide requested data, accessible points of contact or valid phone numbers could result in a firm being considered less qualified. FACTOR 4: QUALITY CONTROL (10 Maximum Points) Subfactor 4A: Management approach (5 Points). Subfactor 4B: Quality methodology (5 Points). The A/E Firm shall describe its management approach, regarding coordination of disciplines and subcontractors, familiarity of the prime firm and any key subcontractors with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications, ASHRAE standards, NEC, and other applicable standards. A/E Firm shall also provide the following: Quality Control organization, and management structure. Methods and procedures for control and prevention of nonconformances during design, preconstruction, and construction. Methods and procedures for nonconformance remediation at all stages of project. Methods and procedures for control and prevention of cost, and schedule overruns. Summarized schedules for selected three previous design projects that show initial approved project schedule, and any updates to schedule with time extensions. Provide a narrative to describe reasons and justifications for any deviations from initial schedule. Summarized cost estimates for selected three previous design projects that show initial approved total project cost estimate, and any increases to initial cost estimates. Provide a narrative to describe reasons and justifications for any deviations from initial estimates. Describe any unforeseen conditions that arose during construction for your last three projects. Provide a narrative to describe how your firm assisted the project management team to correct those deficiencies, and any methods used to mitigate extra costs and increases in project schedule. FACTOR 5: CAPACITY (10 Maximum Points) Subfactor 5A: Capacity to complete work within required timeline (5 Points). Subfactor 5B: Resource management and project management (5 Points). The A/E Firm shall attest to its capacity to accomplish the work in the required time. The evaluation will consider the firm s ability to meet the schedule of the overall project, as well as the available capacity of personnel in key disciplines. The A/E Firm shall also provide the following: A list that shows the total number of design and project professionals who are currently employed at the firm with professional titles for each. Total number of projects in study or planning stages Total number of active design projects Total number of active construction phase services A list of personnel assigned to each of the above projects An analysis and report of available capacity of key personnel for immediate new work The respondent shall: Summarize its approach to staffing and company resource management For the key personnel on the proposed project team, tabulate their current and projected workload as percentages of their available individual capacity. List all work awarded to the A/E Firm by the VA during the previous 12 months, as well as any current indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contracts that it has. List the current stage and percentage of completion for non-IDIQ projects. A signed statement shall be provided stating that the firm acknowledges that prior to award of the contract, it is required to notify the Government of any changes in its capacity that could limit its ability to perform the work within the required time. FACTOR 6: GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION (5 Maximum Points) Location of the firm, as measured by the travel time (hours) between the Offeror s principal business location and Edward Hines, Jr. VAMC, Hines, IL. Architect must provide details of travel between their main office and Edward Hines Jr, VAMC Hines, IL. This includes but not limited to airport travel time, driving distance, etc. If the architect has a satellite location, the architect must provide details of a fully staffed and well-established satellite office. Leasing documentation may be requested. FACTOR 7: EXPERIENCE IN CONSTRUCTION PERIOD SERVICES (5 Maximum Points) The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its experience in providing Construction Period Services for hospital facilities, particularly in HVAC renovation projects. The respondent shall provide a narrative that describes the methods and procedures used to implement each of the following Construction Period Services tasks: Professional field inspections during the construction period, with descriptions of types of inspections provided, and methods used for inspections and reporting during each phase of construction Review of construction submittals Support in answering requests for information during the construction period Support of construction contract changes to include updated drawings, drafting statements of work, and cost estimates. Weekly construction meeting participation Closeout documents to include final inspections and as-recorded drawings. SECONDARY SELECTION CRITERION*: FACTOR 8: CLAIMS (-5 to 0 Maximum Points) Subfactor 8: Record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. (-5 to 0 Points). * The secondary selection criterion is used as a tiebreaker, if necessary, in ranking the most highly qualified firms following the completion of discussions. The secondary selection criterion will not be applied when determining a firm s SF330 submission. 2.1.c: After TEB Individual Ratings of the SF330s are completed, the TEB shall convene and develop consensus ratings for the seven evaluation factors of the SF330s as defined above. COMMENT DESCRIPTION DEFINITIONS Strong point: Provides Merit/advantages to VA that increase the likelihood of successful contract performance. Weak point: Flaws/disadvantages that increase the likelihood of unsuccessful contract performance. 2.2.c: The eighth factor (Secondary Selection Criterion) will only be used if needed. The TEB shall provide a listing, in order of preference, of the firms considered most highly qualified to perform the work. The contracting officer shall issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) to the architect-engineer the TEB recommends for negotiations. 3. SOURCE SELECTION PROCESS: 3.1 SF330 Reviews: The board will review and evaluate the submitted SF330 s in accordance with the stated evaluation criteria to determine each individual offeror s ability and capability to perform the work required and confirmation of determination of responsibility per FAR 9.1. a) TECHNICAL EVALUATION BOARD SF330 INDIVIDUAL EVALUATIONS (1) Each board member will conduct an independent review and evaluation and complete an evaluation rating sheet for EACH SF330. Each category will be addressed with strengths or weaknesses noted. (2) The evaluation will be in accordance with the Evaluation Factors which are listed in the solicitation. b) TECHNICAL EVALUATION BOARD SF330 CONSENSUS (1) After each member has completed their independent evaluation, the Chairperson will discuss the evaluations with the entire team and assure each evaluation is complete. (2) During these discussions, the board will reach a consensus rating for each SF330 and document ratings using the consensus evaluation worksheets. The SF330 can be downloaded through the GSA Forms Library at: https://www.gsa.gov/forms-library/architect-engineer-qualifications. No Fax Responses will be accepted: personal visits for discussing this announcement will not be entertained or scheduled. Questions may be directed only by e-mail to Donita.Grace@va.gov. VA Primary Point of Contact: Donita Grace, NCO 12 Contract Specialist, Donita.Grace@va.gov. The page limit for SF330 s will be 30 pages max., any pages after 30 will not be considered. See attached document: P01 - SOW 578-27-003 Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1

postings.description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT notice; a market survey for information only, to be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information or industry response to this notice or any follow up information requests. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future procurement. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in the System for Award Management (SAM). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor SAM for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The acquisition strategy will be determined based on responses received from this notice and/or other market research methods. The planned acquisition strategy will be posted in SAM upon completion of market research analysis. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of industry, to include the Small Business Community: Small Disadvantage Business (SDB), the 8(a) Program, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), or Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). All are highly encouraged to respond. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, intends to solicit and award a contract to construct a UEPH Barracks at Fort Hood. The anticipated acquisition will be competitive, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Design-Bid-Build (DBB), definitive contract. The procurement will be conducted in accordance with RFO 15.103-1, using the Best Value, Tradeoff Process approach. The Government is seeking experienced construction firms to construct UEPH barracks at Fort Hood, Texas. The project will provide permanent party housing for 250 Soldiers in closer proximity to existing unit headquarters and motor pools. The facility will be designed in accordance with current Army standard barracks design criteria. Primary facilities include living and sleeping quarters, bathrooms, storage areas, service areas, a dayroom, a self-contained heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system, building information systems, antiterrorism measures, fire protection and alarm systems, Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV), Energy Monitoring and Control Systems (EMCS) connections, and special foundations. The estimated air-conditioning capacity is 260 tons. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, exterior lighting, paving, waterway road and pedestrian crossings, parking, sidewalks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping, and signage. The project will include Post-Construction Award Services (PCAS) and comprehensive interior design services related to the building and furnishings. The facility will incorporate accessibility features for individuals with disabilities, cybersecurity measures, sustainability and energy-efficiency measures, and antiterrorism features in accordance with applicable Department of Defense (DoD) minimum antiterrorism standards for buildings. The facility will be designed for a minimum service life of 40 years in accordance with DoD Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 1-200-02, including applicable requirements for energy efficiency, building envelope performance, and integrated building systems. The target price range for this project is between $99,000.00 and $121,000,000. The estimated Period of Performance is 1,000 calendar days. The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, which has a small business size standard of $45.0M. The Product Service Code is Y1FC – Construction of Troop Housing Facilities Respondents are reminded that all construction performance must follow the USACE Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1), and must also comply with all Federal, State and local laws, ordinances, codes and/or regulations. Anticipated solicitation may be issued within 2nd Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 with an estimated award of 4th Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Small Businesses are reminded that RFO clause 52.219-14 – Limitations on Subcontracting will be applicable to this contract; and to pay specific attention to paragraphs (e)(3) and (g). (e)(3) For General Construction, it (the contractor) will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor's 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. (g) A joint venture agrees that, in the performance of the contract, the applicable percentage specified in paragraph (e) of this clause will be performed by the aggregate of the joint venture participants. (1) In a joint venture comprised of a small business protégé and its mentor approved by the Small Business Administration, the small business protégé shall perform at least 40 percent of the work performed by the joint venture. Work performed by the small business protégé in the joint venture must be more than administrative functions. (2) In an 8(a) joint venture, the 8(a) participant(s) shall perform at least 40 percent of the work performed by the joint venture. Work performed by the 8(a) participants in the joint venture must be more than administrative functions The Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) is the Department of Defense, single, authorized application to retrieve supplier performance information. postings.description: Title:Â Temporary Operations and Maintenance Staffing Services for Skilled Trades Louisville VA Medical Center, Kentucky Agency:Â Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Place of Performance: New Louisville VA Medical Center, 4906 Brownsboro Road, Louisville, KY 40222 Robley Rex VA Medical Center, 800 Zorn Avenue, Louisville, KY 40206-1433 Other VA locations within the Louisville VAMC catchment area, as required Description The Department of Veterans Affairs is conducting market research to identify capable and qualified businesses that can provide temporary operations and maintenance staffing services for the Louisville VA Medical Center during facility activation, commissioning, and ongoing operations. The anticipated requirement supports patient care, life-safety systems, and mission-essential healthcare infrastructure. The contractor would recruit, screen, employ, supervise, and provide qualified personnel to perform facility operations, maintenance, repair, inspection, testing, troubleshooting, commissioning support, and related work.Â Contractor personnel will not perform inherently governmental functions. The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month base period with up to two 1-year option periods.Â This notice is issued solely for market-research and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Anticipated Labor Categories and Estimated Staffing The Government anticipates a need for the following labor categories. Quantities are estimates only and do not guarantee a minimum level of effort. Labor Category Estimated FTEs Utility Systems Repairer-Operator (USRO) 8 Maintenance Mechanic (Multi-Trade) 4 Pipefitter / Plumber 3 HVAC Mechanic 4 Scope Highlights Potential contractors must be able to provide personnel qualified to support commercial, institutional, industrial, or healthcare facility systems.Â Services may include preventive and corrective maintenance, utility plant operations, HVAC and refrigeration work, plumbing and pipefitting, general multi-trade maintenance, emergency response, and documentation of completed work in the Government s computerized maintenance management system. Key requirements include: Staffing personnel capable of supporting weekdays, evenings, nights, weekends, holidays, rotating shifts, emergency call-back, and, for USRO personnel, continuous 24-hour/7-day coverage as assigned. Providing qualified candidates for routine staffing requirements within 10 business days and, when commercially reasonable, critical vacancies within 5 business days. Replacing personnel within 10 business days unless otherwise approved; immediate removal may be required for safety, security, conduct, or performance reasons. Providing all essential trade tools, testing equipment, uniforms, personal protective equipment, supervision, training, and labor-related costs within fully burdened labor rates. Complying with applicable Federal, VA, OSHA, NFPA, infection-control, life-safety, Lockout/Tagout, and facility-specific requirements. Minimum Personnel Qualifications All proposed personnel must have relevant trade experience, qualifications, licenses, certifications, and demonstrated competency for the assigned labor category.Â Personnel must be able to communicate effectively in English; possess a valid REAL ID-compliant identification; complete VA background investigation requirements; obtain and maintain a Personal Identity Verification badge; and meet applicable VA occupational-health requirements. Additional representative qualifications include: USRO:Â At least 3 years of utility plant operations and maintenance experience, including systems such as boilers, chilled water plants, cooling towers, pumps, heat exchangers, domestic water, compressed air, and related controls.Â Healthcare experience is preferred. HVAC Mechanic:Â EPA Section 608 Universal Certification and at least 3 years of commercial, industrial, institutional, or healthcare HVAC experience.Â Experience with AHUs, VAV systems, chillers, cooling towers, BAS/DDC controls, and refrigeration systems is required. Pipefitter/Plumber:Â At least 3 years of relevant experience and journeyman-level pipefitting, plumbing, or mechanical-piping experience.Â Experience with domestic water, sanitary systems, steam, condensate, chilled water, heating hot water, and gas piping is required. Maintenance Mechanic (Multi-Trade):Â At least 3 years of commercial, industrial, institutional, or healthcare maintenance experience and journeyman-level experience in building, industrial, or mechanical maintenance.Â Medical gas maintenance certification is preferred when medical-gas work is assigned. Security, Training, and Compliance Before assignment, contractor personnel will be subject to Government review and approval and must complete required documentation, background investigation and credentialing actions, VA New Employee Orientation, safety and infection-control training, and other required training.Â The contractor must maintain a drug-free workplace and ensure compliance with VA privacy, information-security, records-management, and occupational-health requirements. Requested Capability Statement Interested parties should submit a capability statement that addresses the firm s ability to perform this requirement. Include: Business identification:Â Company name, UEI, CAGE code, business address, website, and primary point of contact. Socioeconomic status:Â Identify all applicable SBA socioeconomic designations, including small business, SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB/EDWOSB, and small disadvantaged business status. Relevant experience:Â Describe recent and relevant contracts providing temporary skilled-trades staffing or operations and maintenance support for healthcare, institutional, industrial, or similarly critical facilities.Â Include customer, contract number, period of performance, scope, labor categories, staffing levels, and contract value. Recruiting and retention capacity:Â Describe the ability to recruit, screen, credential, onboard, and retain qualified USROs, HVAC mechanics, pipefitters/plumbers, and multi-trade maintenance mechanics in the Louisville, Kentucky labor market. Response and replacement capability:Â Explain the firm s ability to meet the anticipated candidate-submission and personnel-replacement timeframes. Compliance approach:Â Summarize processes for credential verification, licensing and certification tracking, background investigations, PIV credentialing, occupational-health compliance, training, PPE and tool management, electronic timekeeping, and monthly compliance reporting. Pricing information:Â Provide nonbinding, fully burdened hourly labor-rate ranges for each anticipated labor category. Rates should account for wages, fringe benefits, taxes, insurance, overhead, profit, supervision, tools, PPE, training, overtime, holiday pay, shift differentials, and other labor-related costs. Contracting approach:Â Identify whether the firm would perform as a prime contractor, use subcontractors, or both. If subcontractors are anticipated, identify their roles and relevant capabilities. NAICS Code The Government anticipates that an appropriate NAICS code may beÂ 561320, Temporary Help Services, with a corresponding small-business size standard to be confirmed before any solicitation.Â Respondents may recommend a more appropriate NAICS code and provide supporting rationale. Response Instructions Submit capability statements electronically in PDF format. Responses should be concise and should not exceed 10 pages, excluding resumes and supporting certifications. Response Due Date: November 09, 2026, No Later Than 1100 CST Submission Email: scott.dickey@va.gov Subject Line:Â Sources Sought Response Temporary O&M Skilled Trades Staffing Louisville VAMC Disclaimer This notice is for planning and market-research purposes only. It is not a solicitation, does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, and does not authorize reimbursement of costs incurred in preparing a response. Any future solicitation, if issued, will be posted separately on SAM.gov. Bracketed fields should be completed by the contracting office before posting. Â

postings.description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE for a Market Research ONLY to determine the availability of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential future acquisition. The purpose of this NOTICE is to gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following categories: Small Business, Certified 8a, Certified HUB Zone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), for a Service Contract for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), San Francisco District. The capabilities will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining to Set-Aside for the Small Business Community or to conduct as an Other Than Small Business Procurement. Other than small businesses may respond to this NOTICE in the event the market does not indicate SB interest, however, preference will be given to the SB categories listed above. The government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Contractor shall provide all manpower, labor, equipment, materials/supplies, transportation, fuel, tools, supervision and other items and services necessary to provide sewage pumping and proper disposal, drain clearing, portable toilet rental, and portable/vault toilet stall cleaning/treatment services for the recreation areas designated for public use at Coyote Valley Dam and Lake Mendocino in Ukiah, California. The Period of Performance is anticipated to be 1 Base Year and 3 Option years. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or around December 2026. An official synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on beta.sam.gov and inviting firms to register electronically to receive a copy of the solicitation when it is issued. Requirements Overview 5.1 Basic Services: Sewage pumping and drain clearing is directly related to public health and sanitation and is essential to CVD/ Lake Mendocino’s recreation mission. The Contractor shall furnish all equipment, supplies, items, labor, materials, and services necessary to for sewage pumping and proper disposal, drain clearing, portable toilet rental, and portable/vault toilet stall cleaning/treatment in accordance with all federal, state, and local regulations. 5.2 Service Descriptions: 5.2.1 Lift Stations & Holding Tanks: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank (including all litter and refuse such as bottles, trash bags, clothing, etc.), and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Tank capacities throughout the park vary from 1,000 – 10,000 gallons. Tank locations are outlined in Attachment 1 Work Site Area & Sewage Locations. 5.2.2 Vault Toilets: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each tank/vault. This includes all litter and refuse (bottles, cans, trash bags, clothing, etc.), which can be a common occurrence in the public vault toilets at Lake Mendocino. The Contractor shall also recharge the tank/vault with approximately one foot of water after pumping, apply an enzyme treatment if needed, and hose down the area around the tank ensuring any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. An enzyme treatment may be needed to control odor and maintain cleanliness of the stall. The removed waste shall be transported from CVD/ Lake Mendocino and disposed of in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Contractor shall bear all cost in connection with this work. Vault toilets have a capacity of 1,000 gallons per stall. Vault toilet locations are outlined in Attachment 1. 5.2.3 Sewer and Drain Line Clearing: The Contractor shall provide any combination of video camera services, snaking, rooting, hydro-jetting, and/or chemical treatment necessary to identify and remedy drain line clogs such that the lines can flow freely. Lines that do not continue to flow freely for one week (7 days) will require re-work at no additional cost to the Government. 5.2.4 Portable Toilets: 5.2.4.1 Amount, Type, and Condition: Locations subject to portable toilet placement include recreation areas outlined in Attachment 1. This will primarily be in areas with flush restrooms that occasionally experience system failures. The Contractor shall have enough inventory 15 available to be able to provide up to four (4) sets of portable toilets at one time. A set includes one regular size portable toilet and one ADA-compliant size portable toilet. Portable toilets shall be for outdoor-use and anchorable. The Contractor shall maintain portables that are clean and in good repair, free of significant odors, damage, and vandalism. Stalls must have adequate ventilation, be uniformly painted, constructed such that walls provide adequate privacy, and have doors with a working lock mechanism. Portables should be delivered and placed on flat, level ground surfaces as directed by the COR. In the event portables are vandalized, damaged, and/or moved by the public, the Contractor bears the responsibility of retrieving, repairing and/or replacing them. At the discretion of the COR, the Contractor shall remove and replace damaged portables with ones in good condition. There are also two (2) USACE-owned portable toilets that are subject to service. The Contractor is not responsible for the good working condition of these portables but is required to follow the same service description outlined below in Section 5.2.4.3 for the same unit price as the Contractor-owned portables. 5.2.4.2 Rental Period: The Contractor shall deliver portable toilets in good working conditions within 48 hours of request by the COR. Portable toilets will be rented per type per two-week (15-day) period. 5.2.4.3 Service: The Contractor shall pump/remove all solid and liquid material from each portable, transport the waste from CVD/ Lake Mendocino, and dispose of it in accordance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Additionally, each portable should be recharged with an industry standard deodorant/cleaner, restocked with reasonably enough toilet paper to last until the next service, and thoroughly cleaned. Cleaning includes scrubbing, wiping, rinsing, removing with appropriate soaps, disinfectants, and cleaning solutions to ensure stall floors, walls, ceilings, door, toilet lids, and toilet risers are free from waste, refuse, residues, spider webs, and significant odors. The area should be hosed down around the portables if needed to ensure any spilled material is removed and the area is left clean, sanitary, and safe. 5.3 Frequency: The Contractor shall provide services on a call-out basis. Scheduling for services will be agreed upon between the Contractor and the COR prior to the delivery of services. The allotted quantities for each service per this contract are based on field experiences from the past five (5) years and best estimates for future needs. An example schedule can be found in Attachment 2 Sample Service Schedule. 5.4 Line Items: 1) Lift Station/Holding Tank Pumping | Unit: Gallon a. Offerors should provide a quote per gallon of sewage pump, incorporating any additional costs (litter removal, sewage disposal) into the per gallon quote. 2) Vault Toilet Pumping & Treatment | Unit: Gallon a. Offerors should provide a quote per gallon of sewage pump, incorporating any additional costs (litter removal, recharging/treatment services, sewage disposal) 16 into the per gallon quote. 3) Sewer and Drain Line Clear Out | Unit: Job a. Offerors should provide a quote for a total annual dollar amount that estimates seventeen (17) line clears that involve snaking/rooting/chemical treatment only, and three (3) line clears that require video camera and hydro-jetting services. 4) Portables Pumping & Cleaning | Unit: Each a. Offerors should provide a quote per each pumping/cleaning service trip. 5) Biweekly Rental Regular Portable | Unit: Each a. Offerors should provide a quote per two-week rental period for a regularly sized portable toilet, incorporating any costs necessary for maintaining the stall in good working condition. 6) Biweekly Rental ADA Portable | Unit: Each a. Offerors should provide a quote per two-week rental period for a ADA-compliant sized portable toilet, incorporating any costs necessary for maintaining the stall in good working condition. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS FOR RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Please provide in your response to the following. The submission is limited to no more than 5 pages. Offeror's name, address, point of contact, email address, and phone number. 1. Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when issued. 2. CAGE code and DUNS number if available. 3. Offeror's type of small business and Business Size (small business, 8(a), HUBZone, veteran owned small business, woman owned small business, or SDVOSB). 4. Offeror's Statement of capability (SOC) - include a statement demonstrating: The skills, equipment, and personnel required to perform the specified type of services are available, or can become available if the contract is awarded. Recent and relevant experience in providing sewage and septic services. The contractor should submit at least 2 examples from the last 5 years. • All interested contractors should notify this office in writing via email by 12:00 PM Pacific Time on 20 February 2023. Submit response and information: via EMAIL to laura.clasen@usace.army.mil and nairi.freeman@usace.army.mil. RESULT INFORMATION: Respondents will NOT be notified of the results of the evaluation. Firms responding to this sources sought notice, who fail to provide all the required information requested, will not be used to help by the government to make the acquisition decision, which is the intent of this sources sought announcement

postings.description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors’ capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The Contractor must demonstrate technical capability conducting Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) bench-, pilot-, or full-scale efficacy evaluations targeting PFAS breakthrough and mass removal kinetics with preferred experience evaluating and optimizing existing pump-and-treat groundwater treatment plants (GWTPs) for PFAS removal across carbon bed changeout cycles, including influent/effluent/interstage monitoring, empty bed contact time (EBCT) assessment, competitive adsorption dynamics with co-contaminants (e.g., VOCs), and bed life forecasting. 4. Reporting & CERCLA Deliverables UFP-QAPP Addenda: The Contractor must optimized worksheets conforming to Intergovernmental Data Quality Task Force (IDQTF) standards for subsequent UPF-QAPP addenda adhering to Army Agency and DOW PFAS policies as issued. Remedial Investigation (RI) Report: Comprehensive documentation satisfying CERCLA § 104(b) and NCP 40 CFR § 300.430(d): Physical site characterization, hydrogeologic cross-sections, and Conceptual Site Models (CSM) (40 CFR § 300.430(d)(2)) including 3D lithologic and chemical plume fate-and-transport modeling. Baseline Risk Assessment comprising both a Baseline Human Health Risk Assessment (BHHRA) and a Baseline Ecological Risk Assessment (BERA) pursuant to 40 CFR § 300.430(d)(4). Stakeholder presentations support for the BRAC Cleanup Team (BCT) and community public meetings. Feasibility Study (FS): Development of remedial alternatives and screening against the nine NCP criteria pursuant to 40 CFR § 300.430(e)–(f), demonstrating compliance with CERCLA § 121 (42 U.S.C. § 9621) cleanup standards and Applicable or Relevant and Appropriate Requirements (ARARs). CAPABILITY STATEMENT The following requests are designed to inform the US Army Corps of Engineers, Sacramento District, of current service contractor market capabilities. Please provide your response to the following. The submission is limited to 10 pages. 1) Offeror's name, Unique Entity Identifier (ID), CAGE Code, address, point of contact, phone number, and e-mail address. 2) Offeror's experience and capability to complete (either through self-performance or the managing of one or more subcontracts as a Prime) contracts of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years. Describe the Prime’s self-performed effort, brief description of the project, customer name, period of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project. 3) Offeror's socioeconomic type and business size (Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns). The Capabilities Statement will not be considered an offer (proposal) or a bid for any future Request for Quotes/Proposal that may result from this notice. Moreover, it will not restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. This notice is for information and planning purposes only. The respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted of the capability statements received. All capability statements must be submitted electronically via email no later than 30 November 2026, 10AM Pacific Standard Time (PST). Submit response to the following Point of Contacts: Davina Darden at davina.d.darden@usace.army.mil and Steven Griffiths steven.j.griffiths@usace.army.mil. Please include the Sources Sought No. W9123826X1CUS in the subject line.
